title: Compound assignment casts
text: `byte b = 10; b += 5;` compiles because `+=` casts back to `byte`. `b = b + 5;` does **not** compile: `b + 5` is an `int`.

title: Integer cache
text: `Integer a = 127, b = 127;` then `a == b` is `true` (cached -128..127). With `128` it is `false`. Compare wrappers with `equals`.

title: Math.round return type
text: `Math.round(double)` returns `long`, `Math.round(float)` returns `int`. `Math.round(-2.5)` is `-2` (rounds half up).

title: Strings are immutable
text: `s.concat("x");` or `s.toUpperCase();` without assigning the result changes nothing.

title: StringBuilder equals
text: `StringBuilder` does not override `equals`, so two builders with the same text are not equal. Compare `sb.toString()` or use `compareTo` (Java 11+).

title: strip vs trim
text: `strip()` removes all Unicode whitespace; `trim()` only removes chars ≤ `\u0020`. Also `stripLeading()`, `stripTrailing()`, `isBlank()`.

title: substring end is exclusive
text: `"hello".substring(1, 3)` is `"el"`. `"hello".substring(5)` is `""`, but `substring(6)` throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

title: Text block indentation
text: The least-indented line (including the closing `"""`) sets the margin that is stripped. Trailing spaces are removed; `\s` keeps a space, `\` at line end joins lines.

title: Text block must start on a new line
text: `"""abc"""` does not compile: the content must start on the line after the opening `"""`.

title: String pool
text: Literals are pooled: `"a" == "a"` is `true`, `new String("a") == "a"` is `false`. `intern()` returns the pooled instance.

title: StringBuilder methods mutate
text: `sb.append("a").reverse()` changes `sb` itself. `delete(start, end)` excludes `end`; `insert(i, x)` shifts the rest right.

title: Date-time is immutable
text: `date.plusDays(1);` without assigning does nothing. Every `plus`/`minus`/`with` returns a new object.

title: Invalid dates fail at runtime
text: `LocalDate.of(2024, 2, 30)` compiles but throws `DateTimeException`. Months are 1–12 (or `Month.FEBRUARY`).

title: Period vs Duration
text: `Period` is years/months/days for dates; `Duration` is hours/minutes/seconds for times. Adding a `Period` to a `LocalTime` throws `UnsupportedTemporalTypeException`.

title: Switch expressions must be exhaustive
text: A `switch` **expression** must cover every value: all enum constants, all permitted sealed subtypes, or a `default`. Otherwise it does not compile.

title: yield, not return
text: In a switch expression, a `{ }` block after `->` must end with `yield value;`. `return` cannot be used to give the expression a value.

title: Unreachable after break
text: A statement directly after `break;`, `continue;`, `return;` or `throw` in the same block is unreachable and does not compile.

title: Labeled break and continue
text: `outer: for (...) { for (...) { break outer; } }` leaves both loops. `continue outer;` jumps to the next iteration of the outer loop.

title: do-while runs once
text: The body of `do { } while (cond);` runs at least once, and the `;` after `while (cond)` is required.

title: Eligible for GC
text: An object is eligible once no live reference can reach it. `System.gc()` is only a suggestion, and `finalize()` is deprecated and may never run.

title: Islands of isolation
text: Two objects that only reference each other but nothing live references them are both eligible for garbage collection.

title: Creating inner class objects
text: An inner class needs an outer instance: `Outer.Inner in = outer.new Inner();`. A static nested class does not: `new Outer.Nested()`.

title: Local classes capture effectively final
text: Local and anonymous classes (like lambdas) can only use local variables that are final or effectively final.

title: Default constructor only if none
text: The compiler adds a no-arg constructor only when the class declares **no** constructor. A subclass relying on implicit `super()` then fails if the parent only has `Parent(int)`.

title: this() or super() comes first
text: A constructor can start with `this(...)` or `super(...)`, not both, and it must be the first statement.

title: Initialization order
text: Superclass first. Static fields and static blocks run once, top to bottom, when the class loads. Then per object: instance fields and instance blocks in order, then the constructor body.

title: Compact record constructor
text: A compact constructor has no parameter list. It can validate or reassign the **parameters**; the fields are assigned after it. Assigning `this.x` inside it does not compile.

title: Records are final
text: Records are implicitly final with `private final` fields. They can implement interfaces and add static fields or methods, but cannot extend a class or add instance fields.

title: Overload resolution order
text: The compiler tries, in order: exact match, widening, boxing, then varargs. The first phase that finds a method wins.

title: Widening beats boxing
text: With `m(long)` and `m(Integer)`, the call `m(5)` picks `m(long)`: widening is tried before boxing.

title: No widening after boxing
text: `m(Long x)` cannot take `m(5)`: an `int` is never boxed to `Integer` and then widened to `Long`. It does not compile.

title: Boxing then widening to Object
text: `m(Object o)` accepts `m(5)`: `int` boxes to `Integer`, which is an `Object`.

title: Return type does not overload
text: Two methods that differ only in return type do not compile. Overloads must differ in parameter types, count or order.

title: Varargs must be last
text: Only one varargs parameter is allowed and it must be last. `void m(int... a, String s)` does not compile.

title: Empty varargs
text: `m()` can call `m(int... a)`; `a` is an empty array, not `null`.

title: int[] and int... clash
text: `m(int[] a)` and `m(int... a)` have the same signature, so declaring both does not compile.

title: Most specific with null
text: With `m(Object)` and `m(String)`, `m(null)` picks `m(String)`. With `m(String)` and `m(StringBuilder)`, `m(null)` is ambiguous and does not compile.

title: Overloads are chosen at compile time
text: The overload is picked from the declared (static) type of the argument. Overrides are picked at runtime from the object's actual type.

title: char widens to int
text: With only `m(int)` and `m(Object)`, `m('a')` calls `m(int)`: widening a `char` beats boxing it to `Character`.

title: Erasure clash
text: `m(List<String>)` and `m(List<Integer>)` both erase to `m(List)`, so they do not compile together.

title: Static and instance with same signature
text: A class cannot have a static method and an instance method with the same name and parameters.

title: var needs an initializer
text: `var x;` and `var x = null;` do not compile: the type must be inferable from a non-null initializer.

title: var is for locals only
text: `var` works for local variables, enhanced-for variables and try-with-resources, but not for fields, method parameters or return types.

title: var and array initializers
text: `var a = {1, 2};` does not compile. `var a = new int[]{1, 2};` does.

title: var is a reserved type name
text: `int var = 3;` compiles because `var` is not a keyword, but you cannot name a class or interface `var`.

title: var type is fixed
text: `var x = 1; x = 2.5;` does not compile: `x` was inferred as `int`.

title: No multiple declarators with var
text: `var a = 1, b = 2;` does not compile. `int a = 1, b = 2;` does.

title: Block scope
text: A variable declared inside an `if` or loop block is gone after the block. A local cannot redeclare another local in scope, but it can shadow a field.

title: Immutable class recipe
text: Make the class final (or constructors private), fields `private final`, no setters, and defensively copy mutable inputs and anything you return.

title: final is not immutable
text: `final List<String> l = new ArrayList<>(); l.add("x");` compiles. `final` only stops reassigning the reference.

title: Access levels
text: `private` < package-private (no modifier) < `protected` < `public`. `protected` adds subclasses in other packages, but only through inheritance.

title: Static methods hide
text: A static method with the same signature in a subclass hides the parent's. Which one runs depends on the reference type, not the object.

title: Fields are not polymorphic
text: `Parent p = new Child(); p.name` reads `Parent`'s field even if `Child` declares its own `name`.

title: What interfaces can contain
text: Abstract methods, `default` methods, `static` methods, and `private` / `private static` helper methods (Java 9+).

title: Interface fields are constants
text: Interface fields are implicitly `public static final` and must be initialized where declared.

title: Static interface methods are not inherited
text: Call them as `MyInterface.m()`. Calling through an implementing class or an instance does not compile.

title: Default method conflict
text: If a class gets the same default method from two interfaces, it must override it. It can call one with `A.super.m()`.

title: Class wins over interface
text: A method inherited from a superclass beats an interface default method with the same signature.

title: Functional interface rule
text: Exactly one abstract method. Public `Object` methods like `equals` or `toString` declared abstract do not count. `@FunctionalInterface` is optional but makes the compiler check.

title: Core functional interfaces
text: `Supplier<T>.get()`, `Consumer<T>.accept(t)`, `Predicate<T>.test(t)`, `Function<T,R>.apply(t)`, `UnaryOperator<T>`, `BinaryOperator<T>`, plus `Bi...` versions.

title: Primitive functional names
text: `IntFunction<R>` takes an `int` and returns `R`. `ToIntFunction<T>` takes `T` and returns `int` via `applyAsInt`. `IntSupplier` uses `getAsInt()`.

title: Lambda parameter names
text: A lambda parameter cannot reuse the name of a local variable in the enclosing scope, and captured locals must be effectively final.

title: var in lambda parameters
text: `(var x, var y) -> x + y` is fine, but mixing `var` with explicit types or untyped parameters does not compile.

title: Four method reference kinds
text: Static `Math::abs`, bound instance `str::length`, unbound instance `String::length`, and constructor `ArrayList::new`.

title: Implementations must be public
text: Interface methods are implicitly public, so an implementing method without `public` reduces visibility and does not compile.

title: What an enum is
text: Constants are implicitly `public static final`. An enum implicitly extends `java.lang.Enum`, so it cannot extend another class.

title: Enum constructors are private
text: Enum constructors are implicitly private. `new Color()` does not compile anywhere.

title: Semicolon after constants
text: When an enum has fields, constructors or methods, the constant list must end with `;`.

title: values, valueOf, ordinal
text: `values()` returns a new array in declaration order. `valueOf("RED")` is case-sensitive and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for unknown names. `ordinal()` starts at 0.

title: Case labels for enums
text: Use `case RED`. Java 21 also allows the qualified `case Color.RED`. The selector itself can be `null` only with a `case null` label.

title: compareTo uses ordinal
text: Enums implement `Comparable` by declaration order, not by name, and are also `Serializable`.

title: Constant-specific bodies
text: A constant can have its own body overriding methods. If the enum declares an `abstract` method, every constant must implement it.

title: Compare enums with ==
text: Each constant is a singleton, so `==` is safe and null-safe. `equals` is final in `Enum`.

title: Exhaustive enum switch
text: A switch expression on an enum needs no `default` if it lists every constant.

title: EnumMap and EnumSet
text: Fast, ordered collections keyed by enum constants, e.g. `EnumSet.of(MON, TUE)` or `new EnumMap<>(Day.class)`.

title: Enums can implement interfaces
text: An enum can implement interfaces, but no class can extend an enum.

title: Static fields in enum constructors
text: An enum constructor cannot read the enum's non-constant static fields: they are not initialized yet, so it does not compile.

title: name() vs toString()
text: `name()` is final and returns the declared name. `toString()` returns the same by default but can be overridden.

title: Nested enums are static
text: An enum declared inside a class is implicitly static, so no outer instance is needed.

title: Streams are lazy
text: Without a terminal operation, intermediate operations like `map` or `peek` never run.

title: A stream is single-use
text: Using a stream after a terminal operation throws `IllegalStateException`.

title: Optional basics
text: `orElse(x)` always evaluates `x`; `orElseGet(supplier)` only when empty. `get()` on an empty Optional throws `NoSuchElementException`.

title: Infinite streams
text: `Stream.iterate` and `Stream.generate` never end without `limit` or a short-circuiting operation. `sorted()` or `count()` on them hangs.

title: map vs flatMap
text: `flatMap` turns `Stream<List<T>>` into `Stream<T>`. `mapToInt` gives an `IntStream`; `boxed()` turns it back into `Stream<Integer>`.

title: IntStream ranges
text: `IntStream.range(1, 5)` excludes 5; `rangeClosed(1, 5)` includes it. `average()` returns `OptionalDouble`; `sum()` returns `int`.

title: javac and java module flags
text: `javac -d out --module-path mods ...`, then `java -p mods -m my.module/com.app.Main`. `-p` is `--module-path`, `-m` is `--module`.

title: Creating a jar
text: `jar --create --file app.jar --main-class com.app.Main -C out .` (short: `jar -cfe app.jar com.app.Main -C out .`).

title: jdeps
text: `jdeps app.jar` lists dependencies; `-s` gives a summary; `--jdk-internals` finds use of internal JDK APIs.

title: jlink
text: `jlink --module-path mods --add-modules my.module --output image` builds a custom runtime. Every module included must be a named module.

title: Unnamed module
text: Jars on the class path form the unnamed module. It can read every module, but named modules cannot `requires` it.

title: Automatic modules
text: A plain jar on the module path becomes an automatic module named from `Automatic-Module-Name` or the file name. It exports all packages and reads all modules.

title: Migration strategies
text: Bottom-up: modularize the lowest dependencies first. Top-down: put everything on the module path as automatic modules, then convert from the top.

title: Single-file launch
text: `java Hello.java` compiles and runs a single source file in memory, no `javac` step.

title: count++ is not atomic
text: `count++` from several threads loses updates. Use `AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet()` or a `synchronized` block.

title: What synchronized locks
text: A synchronized instance method locks `this`; a synchronized static method locks the `Class` object.

title: Unlock in finally
text: Call `lock.unlock()` in `finally`. `tryLock()` returns a `boolean`. Unlocking a lock you don't hold throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`.

title: Liveness problems
text: Deadlock: threads wait on each other forever. Starvation: a thread never gets the resource. Livelock: threads keep reacting to each other but make no progress.

title: volatile
text: `volatile` guarantees visibility of writes across threads, not atomicity of compound actions like `x++`.

title: Iterating a synchronized list
text: With `Collections.synchronizedList(list)`, you must still wrap iteration in `synchronized (list) { ... }`.

title: ConcurrentModificationException
text: Removing from an `ArrayList` inside a for-each throws `ConcurrentModificationException`. `CopyOnWriteArrayList` doesn't: its iterator is a snapshot.

title: ConcurrentHashMap
text: No `null` keys or values. `putIfAbsent`, `computeIfAbsent` and `merge` are atomic.

title: CopyOnWriteArrayList
text: Every write copies the array, and iterators never see later changes. Good for read-mostly lists.

title: BlockingQueue
text: `put`/`take` block until possible; `offer`/`poll` with a timeout wait up to it. Common: `LinkedBlockingQueue`, `ArrayBlockingQueue`.

title: forEach on parallel streams
text: `forEach` on a parallel stream has no order; `forEachOrdered` keeps encounter order.

title: findAny in parallel
text: On a parallel stream, `findAny()` can return any element. Use `findFirst()` when order matters.

title: Parallel reduce rules
text: For `reduce(identity, op)` in parallel, the identity must be a true identity and `op` associative, or results differ between runs.

title: Sorted concurrent collections
text: `ConcurrentSkipListMap` and `ConcurrentSkipListSet` are the thread-safe, sorted versions of `TreeMap` and `TreeSet`.

title: Shared state in parallel streams
text: Adding to a shared `ArrayList` from `parallel().forEach` is not thread-safe. Use `collect(...)` instead.

title: Byte vs character streams
text: `InputStream`/`OutputStream` work with bytes; `Reader`/`Writer` with characters.

title: read() returns an int
text: `read()` returns `-1` at end of stream, which is why it returns `int`, not `byte` or `char`.

title: Close order in try-with-resources
text: Resources close in reverse order of declaration, after the try block. Exceptions from `close()` become suppressed if the body already threw.

title: Console can be null
text: `System.console()` returns `null` when there is no console, for example in an IDE.

title: readLine
text: `BufferedReader.readLine()` returns `null` at end of file and drops the line terminator.

title: FileWriter overwrites
text: `new FileWriter(file)` truncates the file; `new FileWriter(file, true)` appends.

title: Serializable is a marker
text: A class must implement `Serializable`, or `writeObject` throws `NotSerializableException` at runtime.

title: transient and static are skipped
text: Neither is serialized. After deserialization, `transient` fields hold their default value (`0`, `null`, `false`).

title: No constructor runs
text: Deserializing runs no constructor of the serializable class. Only the no-arg constructor of the first non-serializable superclass runs, and it must exist.

title: serialVersionUID
text: If the stream's `serialVersionUID` doesn't match the class, reading throws `InvalidClassException`.

title: Every field must be serializable
text: A non-transient field holding a non-serializable object makes `writeObject` throw `NotSerializableException`.

title: readObject needs a cast
text: `ObjectInputStream.readObject()` returns `Object` and can throw `ClassNotFoundException` as well as `IOException`.

title: Records deserialize through the constructor
text: Unlike normal classes, a record is rebuilt via its canonical constructor, so its validation runs.

title: Initializers don't run
text: Field initializers and instance blocks of a serializable class do not run on deserialization.

title: Custom serialization hooks
text: Declare `private void writeObject(ObjectOutputStream)` and `private void readObject(ObjectInputStream)` to customize.

title: Static fields aren't restored
text: Static fields keep whatever value the current JVM has; they are not read from the stream.

title: Path.of and Paths.get
text: Both create a `Path`; `Path.of` is the newer (Java 11) form. Creating a `Path` never touches the file system.

title: resolve with an absolute path
text: `p.resolve(other)` returns `other` unchanged when `other` is absolute.

title: relativize needs matching types
text: `relativize` needs both paths absolute or both relative, otherwise `IllegalArgumentException`.

title: normalize vs toRealPath
text: `normalize()` removes `.` and `..` without checking the disk. `toRealPath()` checks the disk and throws if the file doesn't exist.

title: Files.delete
text: `Files.delete` throws `NoSuchFileException` if missing and `DirectoryNotEmptyException` for a non-empty folder. `deleteIfExists` returns a `boolean`.

title: Lazy file streams
text: `Files.lines`, `Files.list` and `Files.walk` return lazy streams that should be closed (try-with-resources). `walk` includes the start path.

title: Files.copy won't overwrite
text: `Files.copy` throws `FileAlreadyExistsException` unless you pass `StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING`.

title: Path names exclude the root
text: For `/a/b/c`, `getNameCount()` is 3 and `subpath(0, 1)` is `a` (relative, no root).

title: Creating a Locale
text: `Locale.of("en", "US")` (Java 19+), `new Locale.Builder().setLanguage("en").setRegion("US").build()`, or constants like `Locale.US`. Language is lowercase, country uppercase.

title: NumberFormat kinds
text: `getCurrencyInstance`, `getPercentInstance`, `getIntegerInstance`, and `getCompactNumberInstance(locale, Style.SHORT)`, which formats `1_000_000` as `1M`.

title: ResourceBundle lookup
text: It tries the requested locale, then its language only, then the default locale, then the base bundle with no locale.

title: Missing bundle key
text: `bundle.getString("x")` throws `MissingResourceException` if no bundle in the chain has the key.

title: DateTimeFormatter letters
text: `MM` is month, `mm` minute, `HH` 24-hour, `hh` 12-hour, `a` AM/PM. `ofLocalizedDate(FormatStyle.SHORT)` uses the locale's style.

title: Pattern doesn't fit the type
text: Formatting a `LocalDate` with a pattern containing `HH` or `mm` throws `UnsupportedTemporalTypeException`.

title: MessageFormat
text: `MessageFormat.format("Hi {0}, you have {1} mails", name, n)` fills numbered placeholders.
